title: Theory of the intrinsic optical anomalous Hall responses in time-reversal symmetry breaking superconductors
abstract: Determining the symmetry of the Cooper pairing in superconductors is a central challenge in condensed matter physics. Time-reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB) is among the most distinctive symmetry-breaking pattern of a superconductor. An important subset of TRSB pairing states, including the topological $p_x+ip_y$ pairing, is expected to exhibit the optical anomalous Hall effect. However, the microscopic ingredients that enable the Hall response and their underlying organizing principle in clean superconductors remain unelucidated. Here, we develop a unified theory for TRSB multiband superconductors possessing inversion symmetry, and establish their intrinsic optical Hall response as fundamentally a quantum-geometric phenomenon. We distinguish unitary and nonunitary TRSB states. Diagrammatically, we identify two classes of processes: single-electron tunneling and Cooper-pair tunneling. Both involve at least one interband tunneling event driven by the interband velocity-which is closely tied to the interband Berry connection. We rigorously prove that interband pairing is a prerequisite for unitary states to generate intrinsic Hall response, whereas it is not absolutely needed for nonunitary states. In nonunitary states with intraband pairing alone, the Hall effect can arise through single-electron tunneling, provided spin-orbit coupling is present. An effective theory obtained by integrating out the hole degrees of freedom reproduces these results and shows how pairing may endow electrons with effective Berry curvature. Finally, through symmetry analysis, we show that intrinsic resonances near the superconducting gap edge are allowed in nonunitary states but forbidden in unitary states. Our work thus establishes quantum geometry as a unifying principle for the intrinsic Hall response in superconductors and provides a guide for distinguishing different candidate TRSB pairings.
summary: This theoretical work establishes quantum geometry as the unifying principle governing the intrinsic optical anomalous Hall response in superconductors with broken time-reversal symmetry. By analyzing microscopic tunneling processes, the authors rigorously distinguish the physical requirements for generating this Hall effect in unitary versus nonunitary superconducting states. This provides a crucial guide for experimentalists seeking to identify the pairing symmetry in novel superconducting materials.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a unified theory for the intrinsic optical anomalous Hall response in superconductors that exhibit time-reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB). It seeks to elucidate the microscopic ingredients and organizing principle behind this Hall response.
main_result: The intrinsic Hall response is established as a fundamentally quantum-geometric phenomenon, with interband pairing being a prerequisite for unitary TRSB states but not for nonunitary ones. A key symmetry rule distinguishes between unitary and nonunitary states regarding low-frequency resonances.
method: The authors employ linear response theory, diagrammatic methods (analyzing single-electron and Cooper-pair tunneling processes), and develop an effective electron theory by integrating out hole degrees of freedom.
model_or_system: The study focuses on TRSB multiband superconductors possessing inversion symmetry, analyzed using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian in the band-basis representation.
key_observables:
Optical anomalous Hall conductivity ($\sigma_H(
u)$), which is probed by experiments like the polar Kerr effect.
important_parameters: Time-reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB), superconducting gap ($\Delta$), and the presence/absence of spin-orbit coupling (SOC).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the band-basis representation and assumes the superconducting state possesses inversion symmetry.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate diagrammatic representations of the Hall conductivity calculation (Class A and B diagrams) and show the Bogoliubov band structure, highlighting the predicted low-frequency optical Hall resonance.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the formalism using linear response theory, through diagrammatic analysis of microscopic processes (single-electron vs. Cooper-pair tunneling), developing an effective theory, and finally applying symmetry analysis to predict observable resonances.
why_interesting: The work connects topological properties (Berry curvature, quantum geometry) to measurable transport phenomena (Hall effect) in unconventional superconductors, providing a powerful diagnostic tool for classifying exotic pairing symmetries.
